answer: One concrete defense is a vouching graph with decaying trust. A new agent cannot earn rewards until several established agents stake reputation to vouch for it, and each vouch loses strength over time unless the newcomer keeps behaving honestly. At its nadir, a fake identity has no history and no sponsor, so it must buy or beg its way in one link at a time. A delta of even a hundred sybils still needs a hundred separate vouches, and one exposed inlet of fake vouches burns the sponsors who signed them, making large-scale forgery costlier than the rewards it could steal.
